questions.prompt:
The organiser of SG60 concerts sold tickets over one weekend. Seats were in three sections.

Week 1 ticket sales:
Section A - Saturday 164, Sunday 128
Section B - Saturday 144, Sunday 90
Section C (obstructed view) - Saturday 50, Sunday 40

Write down a 2 x 3 matrix A to represent this information (rows = Saturday, Sunday; columns = A, B, C).
questions.explanation:
Row 1 is Saturday sales for sections A, B, C.
Row 2 is Sunday sales for sections A, B, C.

questions.prompt:
Ticket prices are $30 (Section A), $25 (Section B) and $20 (Section C).

Represent these prices in a 3 x 1 column matrix P.
questions.explanation: Order the prices to match sections A, B, C as a single column.

questions.prompt:
Using
A = [[164, 144, 50], [128, 90, 40]]
and
P = [[30], [25], [20]],

evaluate the matrix (1 1)AP and interpret the element(s) in the resulting matrix.
questions.model_answer:
(16410)

This element is the total amount collected from ticket sales on Saturday and Sunday combined in week 1.
questions.explanation:
AP = [[9520], [6890]] (Saturday and Sunday revenue).
(1 1)AP = 9520 + 6890 = 16410, the combined weekend revenue.

questions.prompt:
In week 2, compared with week 1 matrix A:
- Section A sales increase by 25%
- Section B sales increase by 50%
- Section C sales decrease to 80% of the original

Write down a matrix M such that F = AM gives the week-2 Saturday/Sunday sales for sections A, B and C.
questions.explanation: M is a 3 x 3 diagonal scale matrix that multiplies each section column by its week-2 factor.

questions.prompt: With F = AM (week-2 sales) and P the price column matrix, state what each element of matrix FP represents.
questions.model_answer: Each element of FP is the total amount collected from ticket sales on Saturday and on Sunday respectively in week 2.
questions.explanation: FP multiplies week-2 sales by prices, giving daily revenue totals for Saturday and Sunday.

questions.subtopic: Mean and standard deviation from grouped data
questions.prompt:
Waiting times (minutes) for 50 patients at Hospital A:

20 < t <= 24: 8 patients
24 < t <= 28: 10 patients
28 < t <= 32: 21 patients
32 < t <= 36: 7 patients
36 < t <= 40: 4 patients

Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the waiting times in Hospital A.

Hospital A waiting times have mean 29.12 min and SD about 4.47 min.
Hospital B has mean 29.12 min and SD = 3.2 min.

Compare briefly the waiting times for the A&E clinics in both hospitals.
questions.model_answer: Both hospitals have the same mean waiting time (29.12 min), so average waits are similar. Hospital B has a smaller standard deviation (3.2 < 4.47), so waiting times at B are more consistent / less spread out.

questions.prompt:
From the 50 Hospital A patients:
- 8 waited 24 minutes or less (the 20 < t <= 24 class)
- 11 waited more than 32 minutes (7 + 4 in the last two classes)

Two patients are selected at random. Find the probability of selecting one patient who waited 24 minutes or less and the other who waited more than 32 minutes.

Ali and Robert ran a 42 km race. Ali's average speed was x km/h. Robert's average speed was 2 km/h slower than Ali's. Robert finished 30 minutes later than Ali.

Form an equation in x and show that it reduces to x^2 - 2x - 168 = 0.
In the race-speed model, the quadratic x^2 - 2x - 168 = 0 gives solutions x = -12 and x = 14. Explain why one solution must be rejected.
questions.model_answer: x represents average speed, so it cannot be negative. Reject x = -12.
questions.explanation: Speed must be positive; only x = 14 is valid.

questions.prompt: Ali's valid average speed is 14 km/h for a 42 km race. Robert is 2 km/h slower. Calculate the time taken for Robert to complete the race.

Mdm Siti flies Singapore to Doha (7 h 40 min) then Doha to London (6 h 10 min), plus a 2-hour layover. She departs Singapore at 11:15 PM. London is 7 hours behind Singapore.

What is her arrival time in London, in local London time?
questions.explanation:
Total journey time including layover = 13 h 50 min + 2 h = 15 h 50 min.
Singapore arrival clock time: 11:15 pm + 15 h 50 min = 3:05 pm next day.
London local = 3:05 pm - 7 h = 8:05 am.

questions.prompt:
Mdm Siti brings SGD $700. Exchange rate: 1 pound = SGD 1.65. She stays 6 days and plans on average:
- 25 pounds/day food
- 10 pounds/day transport
- 15 pounds/day sightseeing
- plus 10% of SGD 700 for emergencies

By showing working, determine whether SGD $700 is sufficient for meals, transport, sightseeing and emergencies.
questions.explanation:
Daily = 50 pounds => 6 days = 300 pounds => SGD 300 x 1.65 = $495.
Emergencies = 10% of $700 = $70.
Total planned = $565 < $700, so sufficient.

questions.prompt:
Mdm Siti has 60 pounds for 4 days of sightseeing (2 attractions per day). Options:

A: 4-day pass 90 pounds, with 5% discount if she stays more than 5 days in London (she stays 6 days).
B: Pay-as-you-go at 12.50 pounds per attraction.
C: 2-day pass 35 pounds, then 6 pounds per attraction for the other 2 days.

Which option is most cost-effective for her plan? Show calculations and explain.
questions.model_answer: Option C (59 pounds). It covers all 8 attractions and stays within the 60-pound budget; A (85.50) and B (100) both exceed 60.
questions.explanation:
Budget = 15 x 4 = 60 pounds.
A: 90 x 0.95 = 85.50 (over budget).
B: 8 x 12.50 = 100 (over budget).
C: 35 + 4 x 6 = 59 (within budget).
Recommend C.
